chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The camphor, it is the embalming material.

key_terms.الْحَنُوطُ: Embalming mixture, typically of musk and camphor
key_terms.الْكَافُورُ: Camphor, a fragrant substance used in embalming

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the definition of camphor (kafur) used for embalming the deceased?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the terminology of embalming by equating 'kafur' with 'hanut', a fragrant mixture of musk and camphor used to honor the deceased. This definition is crucial for Shia fiqh as it establishes the permissibility and preferred method of preparing the body with aromatic substances, reflecting the Sunnah of enhancing the dignity of the dead. The identification underscores the importance of specific scents in burial rites, linking physical preparation to spiritual respect.
